correctness.rationale: The global face condition follows from acyclic orientations of a cycle; the enlargement by the bipartite graph on plus/minus marks adds only monochromatic cycle vertex covers. Its omitted relative simplices split into two copies of (simplex, Alexander dual of Ind_1(C_n)). A star cover identifies the larger complex with the suspension of the Alexander dual of Ind_2(C_n). Integral relative homology, combinatorial Alexander duality, and published integral wedge-of-spheres types show exactly two possible reduced homology ranks. Distinct ingredient cohomology degrees eliminate connecting map obstructions for n>=6, and free right terms split the integral sequences. The formula agrees with the published 6..21 table, direct GF2 chains n6..9, all filtration words n3..8, and critical-cell calculations Ind_2 n6..22. These finite checks are corroboration, not a replacement for the infinite proof. No torsion or other groups remain.

value.rationale: The authors introducing the strong cycle complex explicitly could not compute the 22-cycle homology and did not find a uniform all-n pattern. The result classifies all integral groups and their torsion-free nature for every n>=6, gives a genuinely uncomputed n22 degree-10 and degree-13 answer, and supplies a reusable structural reduction via two Alexander-dual cycle independence complexes. This goes beyond Euler and face-vector counts and is mathematically motivated by a named gap.
